selection_method: Start from the concrete constraints: small lead-sheet crops, melody plus chord symbols, Humdrum, transposition, independent scoring, persistent goal-directed control. Follow primary project and framework sources; do not rank by multi-agent keyword popularity.

sources.name: Jazzmus / Optical Music Recognition of Jazz Lead Sheets
sources.why_relevant: The task is explicitly melody plus chord symbols at staff level, with **kern and **mxhm output. This is a closer task match than a full-page melody-only path.
sources.verified: Read the paper HTML, official project, repository, inference source and model card. Public code and model checkpoint are available.
sources.limitations: Trained for jazz handwriting and synthetic fonts. Publisher warns about chord errors, implicit accidentals and different printed genres. No performance claim on the church data.
sources.decision: Highest-priority open-source recognition candidate for a subsequent paired benchmark; not installed or run in this investigation.

sources.name: Soundslice
sources.why_relevant: Scans images/PDFs into editable notation, recognizes chord names, transposes, and exports MusicXML. Could already address much of the church workflow.
sources.verified: Read official scanner and supported-notation documentation.
sources.limitations: Vendor capabilities, not an independent accuracy result. Its documented pickup-bar limitation matters for our cropped inputs. Our local .krn chord dialect would need a tested MusicXML conversion.
sources.decision: Useful product comparator. No account created, purchase made, or church data uploaded.

sources.name: ScanScore 3
sources.why_relevant: Official FAQ documents note/lyric/chord recognition, editing, transposition and MusicXML export.
sources.limitations: Not benchmarked on our input; product capability does not establish quality. A .krn conversion remains necessary.
sources.decision: Another product comparator; not purchased or run.

sources.name: LangGraph
sources.why_relevant: Supports separate subgraph message histories through explicit input/output mapping and durable checkpoints. Fits per-agent goals and resumable work.
sources.verified: Read current official subgraph and persistence docs.
sources.limitations: Private state schemas are not OS security boundaries and do not automatically prevent a developer from passing answers. It does not supply a music recognizer or objective.
sources.decision: Good foundation when expanding the prototype. We retained the small existing runner for this controlled review experiment; no claim that a framework migration improves recognition.

sources.name: Inspect AI
sources.why_relevant: Has solvers, separate scorers, deferred scoring, logs and tool sandboxing. Reduces the amount of evaluation plumbing to maintain.
sources.verified: Read official solver, scoring and sandbox docs.
sources.limitations: TaskState exposes target to solver code. Choosing this framework alone does not guarantee blinding. Must deliberately exclude targets from model inputs and tool environments.
sources.decision: Prefer as evaluation infrastructure for larger campaigns after adapting our image provider and music metrics; not installed this turn.

sources.name: Sheet Music Benchmark / OMR-NED
sources.why_relevant: Provides a standard OMR dataset using Humdrum and a metric covering more notation details than our narrow event sequence metric.
sources.verified: Read primary paper abstract/version information; v3 dated July 1, 2026.
sources.limitations: A whole-notation score still does not measure Sunday rehearsal effort or guarantee our chord dialect is supported.
sources.decision: Use as an external comparison metric, while retaining explicit chord timing and musician correction time.

sources.name: Audiveris SCALE documentation
sources.why_relevant: Explains the staff-scale assumptions behind the rejection messages in our logs.
sources.verified: Read official scale-step docs and matched against local logs.
sources.limitations: Explains rejection, not the cause of every later recognition error.
sources.decision: Input geometry is a distinct intervention from model selection.

sources.name: OpenAI evaluation best practices
sources.why_relevant: Supports task-specific measurements, logging, continuous regression evaluation and calibration with human judgments.
sources.limitations: General guidance does not supply a music correctness oracle or isolation mechanism.
sources.decision: Measure observable failures and compare automated scores with musician review.
